summary: The video path is generated at scan time: BG tiles are fetched per pixel from the H/V counters, sprites are scanned per line into a work buffer and then drawn into a line double buffer, and colours are mixed per pixel through the CLUT/palette PROMs. So it does not follow MAME's tilemap/draw_sprites/screen_update decomposition. But the module split is functional (VIDEO/SPRITE/STARGEN/IO/SOUND), not one module per custom chip (CUS20/21/26/29/33/34). The board-specific custom-chip logic (56XX/58XX/62XX I/O, starfield control decode, explosion generator) is closely modelled on MAME's high-level emulation: the CUS2 I/O read is nearly a transliteration of MAME's customio_3_r, the starfield command decoder lists exactly MAME's case values, and the explosion is a PCM sample played on the same write MAME uses to start its sample. The sprite path also carries empirical game-specific flip-screen patches. On balance it leans toward MAME.

findings.note: Offset 0 returns IN2, offsets 1/2/3 return regs/0xF/regs when mode==2, else 0xF/0xE/0x1, and the default returns the stored reg. This is the same switch with the same magic constants as MAME's handler, not a model of the CUS62 chip.
A write to CUS2 offset 9 starts a timer that plays a PCM sample ROM from address 0. That matches MAME's samples->start on offset 0x09, rather than reproducing the 62XX explosion generator.

Each chip is a 16-nibble register file whose contents are rewritten per mode (1 switches, 4/3 coin handling, 8/5 boot check, 9/4 DIP interleave). It uses the same IORAM slot layout as MAME, including the credit BCD/add/sub slots swapped between the two chips (MAME's handle_coins(0) vs (2)) and the even/odd DIP interleave of MAME's mode 9/4.

Blocking assignments update credit_add/credit_sub/credits in sequence (coin <99 increment, start-2 then start-1 decrement gated by reg 9 == 0) inside one clocked block. That is MAME's handle_coins flow written as procedural code, not a 4-bit MCU or gate model.

findings.signal: starfield command lookup of MAME case values
findings.note: Control bytes are decoded by matching the exact set of values MAME enumerates (0x86,0x85,0x06,0x80,0x82,0x81,0x9F,0xAF) into speed/direction, with everything else mapped to stop. A CUS26 would decode register bits, not a list of observed command bytes.

Three 16-bit LFSRs run per pixel, and scrolling is done by pre-stepping the seed forward/backward during vblank. That differs from MAME's precomputed star list, but the generic 0xACE1 seed and taps don't look board-derived either.

Each hblank, attribute RAM is scanned and Y-matched sprites (up to 32) are collected into a work RAM. They are then drawn into a per-line buffer for the next line. That is a per-line hardware-style flow, unlike MAME's per-frame gfx->transmask loop over 64 sprites.

findings.signal: per-pixel BG fetch and PROM mixer
findings.note: Tile code, colour and priority come from VRAM addressed by H/V counter bits, then the char ROM, then CLUT0. Per pixel, the BG-high/opaque and sprite-opaque flags select BG, sprite or star into the palette PROM. MAME draws in layers (stars, low tiles, sprites, high tiles).

Shared RAMs are separate instances sram3I/3J (tilemap) and sram3M/3K/3L (work/sprite), each decoded by its own address compare. That mirrors individual board RAM chips rather than MAME's videoram/spriteram shares.

Ad hoc terms (is_enemy_expl, is_player_beam, beam_fix) keyed on palette numbers, plus tuned X offsets (-88/-75), patch flipped sprites. This is tuning by observation, neither schematic- nor MAME-derived.

The top level splits into SHAREMEM/VIDEO/MAIN/SUB/SOUND. Tile/sprite address generation, sprite generation, line buffer/mixer and timing are not separated into CUS20/21/29/33-style blocks with chip pins.
IRQ-enable and sub-reset latches take their data from A11/A0, and IRQ = enable & VBLK. This is required memory-map behaviour shared by any correct implementation.
